payload.reason: The evidence provides specific details about previously reported results in speculation detection and scope resolution, including performance metrics and comparisons between models.

claims.text: The application of transformer-based architectures (BERT, XLNet, RoBERTa) reported substantial improvements over previously reported results, with at least 0.29 F1 points on cue detection and 4.27 F1 points on scope resolution.
XLNet consistently outperformed BERT and RoBERTa in negation detection and scope resolution, contrary to results on other benchmark datasets.
State-of-the-art results were reported on negation scope resolution for the BioScope Corpus and SFU Review Corpus, with increases of 3.16 F1 points and 0.3 F1 points, respectively.
